- When sentiment is bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism; especially after recent supply events.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior 30d mean), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast growth to 2–3% per day until sentiment stabilizes.
- If official supply net is negative and sentiment is bearish (≤0.33), model often undercorrects — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast mean.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30d windows with high volatility — if forecast is >10% above recent 18d mean, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- When sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish (e.g., 0.67 → 0.33), model often lags — adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- In high-event windows (≥20 events/30d), model tends to overestimate bullishness — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per event beyond 15.
